title.narrative: Innovazione nella gestione delle infrastrutture idriche e sicurezza
SMART WASH – Innovation in the management of water infrastructures and food security in Ethiopia

description.narrative: Aim of the initiative: The project promotes the food security and health of the population in the intervention areas by improving access to safe sources of drinking water, promoting improved hygiene, disseminating sustainable agricultural practices that combine long-term productivity gains with increased resilience of the sector, and supporting the country's digital transition efforts by implementing the use of water management and monitoring software. The partners for the implementation of the project were chosen on the basis of their accumulated experience in the areas of intervention. By exchanging the know-how of each partner, it will be possible to maximise the effectiveness and efficiency of the project in all areas of intervention. Place of intervention: The country of implementation of the initiative is Ethiopia. Two areas of intervention are included: the first includes the Woredas of Geze Gofa, Demba Gofa, Zala and Oyida in the Gofa Zone, within the Southern Ethiopia Region, while the second includes the Woredas of Cheha and Ezha in the Guraghe Zone of the Central Ethiopia Region. Planned activities: To address the identified needs, interventions are planned in three main areas. In order to reduce the spread of water-borne diseases related to the low percentage of population access to water from safe sources (OSS 3.9), the construction or maintenance of drinking water supply systems is envisaged (OSS 6.1 - OECD purpose code 14031). In order to increase long-term sustainability, all interventions will be accompanied by training sessions of local water scheme management and maintenance committees. This will be coupled with training sessions on hygiene and health (OSS 6.2 - OECD purpose code 14032) especially for women. Pertanto, si prevedono interventi di formazione dei contadini sull’adozione di pratiche agricole sostenibili (OSS 2.4 – OCSE purpose code 31120) che possano aumentare la produttività (OSS 2.3) e la resilienza delle comunità al fine di ridurre l’insicurezza alimentare (OSS 2.1). Una particolare attenzione sarà dedicata alle donne che lavorano nell’agricoltura, tramite la creazione o il sostegno di cooperative femminili. A large part of the rural population in the intervention areas live in food-insecure conditions and base their livelihoods on agriculture, which exposes them to severe risks in the event of climate crises or shocks in agricultural input supply chains. Therefore, interventions are foreseen to train farmers in the adoption of sustainable agricultural practices (OSS 2.4 - OECD purpose code 31120) that can increase productivity (OSS 2.3) and community resilience in order to reduce food insecurity (OSS 2.1). It is also envisaged to establish seed banks to preserve and disseminate local seed varieties that are more resilient in the event of climatic anomalies (OSS 2.5). Special attention will be paid to women working in agriculture, through the creation or support of women's cooperatives. The last thematic area of intervention aims to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of drinking water management (OSS 6.4) through capacity building (OSS 6.a - OECD purpose code 14010). In the areas selected for the project, there is a high incidence of non-functioning water schemes, water offices have little knowledge of their territory and limited capacity to intervene. Scopo dell’iniziativa: il progetto promuove la sicurezza alimentare e la salute della popolazione delle aree di intervento migliorando l’accesso a fonti sicure di acqua potabile, promuovendo una maggiore igiene, diffondendo pratiche agricole sostenibili che coniughino l’aumento della produttività sul lungo termine e un incremento della resilienza del settore, e sostenendo gli sforzi di transizione digitale del paese implementando l’uso di un software per la gestione e il monitoraggio delle risorse idriche. I partner per l’implementazione del progetto sono stati scelti sulla base dell’esperienza accumulata nei settori di intervento. Tramite lo scambio del know-how di ogni partner, sarà possibile massimizzare l’efficacia e l’efficienza del progetto in tutti i settori di intervento. Luogo di intervento: il paese di implementazione dell’iniziativa è l’Etiopia. Sono previste due aree di intervento: la prima raggruppa le Woreda di Geze Gofa, Demba Gofa, Zala e Oyida nella Zona Gofa, all’interno della regione della Regione Etiopia Meridionale (Southern Ethiopia Region), mentre la seconda prevede le Woreda di Cheha e Ezha nella Zona Guraghe della Regione Etiopia Centrale (Central Ethiopia Region). Attività previste: per rispondere ai bisogni identificati, si prevedono interventi in tre principali aree tematiche. Per ridurre la diffusione di malattie trasmissibili tramite l’acqua legate alla bassa percentuale di accesso della popolazione all’acqua da fonti sicure (OSS 3.9), si prevede la realizzazione o la manutenzione di impianti di fornitura di acqua potabile (OSS 6.1 – OCSE purpose code 14031). Per aumentarne la sostenibilità sul lungo termine, tutti gli interventi saranno accompagnati da sessioni formative di comitati locali di gestione e manutenzione degli schemi idrici. A ciò si assoceranno delle formazioni in tema di igiene e sanità (OSS 6.2 – OCSE purpose code 14032) destinate in particolare alle donne. Gran parte della popolazione rurale delle aree di intervento vive in condizioni di insicurezza alimentare e basa la sua sussistenza sull’agricoltura, e ciò la espone a pesanti rischi in caso di crisi climatiche o shock nelle catene di approvvigionamento degli input agricoli. Pertanto, si prevedono interventi di formazione dei contadini Allegato 2_Modello Documento Unico di Progetto_DUP_Bando Promossi 2023 7 sull’adozione di pratiche agricole sostenibili (OSS 2.4 – OCSE purpose code 31120) che possano aumentare la produttività (OSS 2.3) e la resilienza delle comunità al fine di ridurre l’insicurezza alimentare (OSS 2.1). Si prevede, inoltre, la creazione di banche dei semi per preservare e diffondere le varietà locali di semenze, maggiormente resilienti in caso di anomalie climatiche (OSS 2.5). Una particolare attenzione sarà dedicata alle donne che lavorano nell’agricoltura, tramite la creazione o il sostegno di cooperative femminili. L’ultima area tematica di intervento punta a migliorare l’efficacia e l’efficienza della gestione delle risorse idriche idropotabili (OSS 6.4) tramite un’attività di capacity building (OSS 6.a – OCSE purpose code 14010). Nelle aree prescelte per il progetto c’è un’elevata incidenza di schemi idrici non funzionanti, gli uffici idrici hanno una scarsa conoscenza del loro territorio e limitate capacità di intervenire. A questo scopo il progetto propone l’introduzione di un software GIS per il censimento e monitoraggio delle risorse idriche (OSS 6.b).

tag.narrative: By 2020, maintain the genetic diversity of seeds, cultivated plants and farmed and domesticated animals and their related wild species, including through soundly managed and diversified seed and plant banks at the national, regional and international levels, and promote access to and fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilization of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, as internationally agreed
By 2030, achieve access to adequate and equitable sanitation and hygiene for all and end open defecation, paying special attention to the needs of women and girls and those in vulnerable situations
By 2030, achieve universal and equitable access to safe and affordable drinking water for all

By 2030, double the agricultural productivity and incomes of small-scale food producers, in particular women, indigenous peoples, family farmers, pastoralists and fishers, including through secure and equal access to land, other productive resources and inputs, knowledge, financial services, markets and opportunities for value addition and non-farm employment
By 2030, end hunger and ensure access by all people, in particular the poor and people in vulnerable situations, including infants, to safe, nutritious and sufficient food all year round

By 2030, ensure sustainable food production systems and implement resilient agricultural practices that increase productivity and production, that help maintain ecosystems, that strengthen capacity for adaptation to climate change, extreme weather, drought, flooding and other disasters and that progressively improve land and soil quality

By 2030, expand international cooperation and capacity-building support to developing countries in water- and sanitation-related activities and programmes, including water harvesting, desalination, water efficiency, wastewater treatment, recycling and reuse technologies

By 2030, substantially increase water-use efficiency across all sectors and ensure sustainable withdrawals and supply of freshwater to address water scarcity and substantially reduce the number of people suffering from water scarcity
By 2030, substantially reduce the number of deaths and illnesses from hazardous chemicals and air, water and soil pollution and contamination
End hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture
Ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all
Ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages
Support and strengthen the participation of local communities in improving water and sanitation management
